t: 3729. Count Distinct Subarrays Divisible by K in Sorted Array
o: Distinct subarrays of a sorted array correspond exactly to choices within maximal runs of equal values — a subarray spanning two different adjacent values is unique to its span anyway, but two equal-valued subarrays can only come from the same run. So for each maximal run of length L with value v, count its subarrays whose sum ≡ 0 (mod k). All elements in a run are equal, so prefix residues advance by v mod k each step; the count is the number of pairs of equal prefix residues, computed with a hash map. Overall O(n).
k: Distinctness reduces to per-run counting because equal content forces the same run.
Within a run, subarray sums divisible by k ↔ pairs of equal prefix residues (prefix sums mod k).

a.i: Walk runs; inside a run maintain running residue m += v (mod k). Before inserting residue m, add the number of earlier prefixes with the same residue (seeded with prefix 0).
s: Scan i; extend j while nums[j] == nums[i].
For each of the (j-i) elements: m = (m + nums[i]) % k; ans += cnt[m]; cnt[m]++.

c.python:
from collections import defaultdict
class Solution:
    def countGoodSubarrays(self, nums: List[int], k: int) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        ans = 0
        i = 0
        while i < n:
            j = i
            while j < n and nums[j] == nums[i]:
                j += 1
            cnt = defaultdict(int)
            cnt[0] = 1
            m = 0
            for _ in range(j - i):
                m = (m + nums[i]) % k
                ans += cnt[m]
                cnt[m] += 1
            i = j
        return ans

a.t: O(n) — each element visited once inside its run
a.sp: O(min(run length, k)) for the residue map

a.n: Approach 2: Closed Form via gcd per Run
a.i: Residues t·v mod k cycle with period p = k / gcd(v, k). In a run of length L, each of the p residue classes appears ⌊L/p⌋ or ⌊L/p⌋+1 times among prefixes 1..L (plus one extra occurrence of residue 0 for the empty prefix). Sum C(c,2) over classes.
s: g = gcd(v, k), p = k / g, q = L // p, r = L % p.
Each class gets q occurrences; the first r classes of the cycle get one more; class 0 gets one extra empty-prefix occurrence.
a.t: O(n log k) — gcd per run

w: Lead with Approach 1 — it generalizes to unsorted arrays (classic subarray-sum-divisible-by-k) whereas the closed form exploits sortedness. Watch overflow: answers reach ~n²/2 ≈ 5·10⁹, use 64-bit. Pitfall: forgetting the seed cnt[0] = 1. Follow-up: count distinct good subarrays in an unsorted array (needs hashing of contents).
